q: How do I add carbon criteria to supplier selection and purchase decisions?
title: Carbon criteria in supplier selection
short: Start with the few categories where most of your purchased emissions sit. Ask suppliers in those categories for document-backed emissions data in every quote, give carbon a fixed weight in your scoring or an internal carbon price in total cost, and write data sharing and reduction expectations into contracts.

p: Rank purchased goods by spend and by a rough emissions estimate. Steel, aluminium, cement, chemicals, plastics and freight usually dominate for manufacturers. Apply carbon criteria to those first; for low impact spend, leave procurement unchanged.

sections.h: Step 2: ask for the data in the quote
ul: Supplier Scope 1 and 2 emissions for the last year, with the invoices or bills behind them.
For key materials, a product carbon footprint per tonne or per unit, with its boundary.
Production route or recycled content where it drives emissions.
p: The GHG Protocol Scope 3 guidance prefers supplier-specific data over averages, so data you collect here also improves your own Scope 3 inventory.

sections.h: Step 3: put carbon into the decision
ul: Weighted scoring: give carbon a fixed share of the technical score and publish it in the tender.
Total cost of ownership: add tonnes x an internal carbon price to each quoted price.
Minimum requirement: for some items, refuse quotes with no emissions data at all.
p: ISO 20400:2017 gives guidance on building sustainability into procurement policy, criteria and contract management.

sections.h: Step 4: write it into the contract
ol: Annual sharing of emissions data in an agreed format.
Notice if the production route or energy source changes.
A reduction expectation, reviewed yearly, rather than a penalty on day one.
Right to see the evidence behind the figures.

example.title: Worked example: two steel quotes with an internal carbon price
lines: Order: 1,000 t of steel; illustrative internal carbon price Rs 1,500 per t CO2e
Supplier A: Rs 55,000 per t, 2.4 t CO2e per t. Price Rs 5.50 crore + carbon 2,400 x 1,500 = Rs 36 lakh. Total Rs 5.86 crore
Supplier B: Rs 56,000 per t, 1.6 t CO2e per t. Price Rs 5.60 crore + carbon 1,600 x 1,500 = Rs 24 lakh. Total Rs 5.84 crore
Supplier B wins by Rs 2 lakh once carbon is priced in
example.note: The carbon price is an internal choice, not a market price. Test the decision at two or three prices.
